Asked only to study English intensifiers, it traced a relay from so to very to really and reproduced two published studies closely.
arxiv-2604-07789: Li and 15 colleagues measure how much different information signals help software-engineering agents succeed. Recent agent workflows first gather intermediate signals during exploration, such as reproduction tests, regression tests, edit locations, execution context, and API usage. No earlier work systematically compares these signals or measures how far agent-found signals lag behind oracle signals. This paper quantifies what oracle signals and agent-extracted signals each contribute to final task success. It also maps the remaining headroom in each signal, showing where better exploration would pay most.
arxiv-2604-07989: Xu and four colleagues build an intent-aware infographic retrieval framework to support authoring. Infographics communicate data-driven stories powerfully, but creating from scratch challenges novices, and finding good exemplars can inspire design and promote reuse. Lookup proves hard because users state design intent in vague natural language while infographics pack rich, multi-part visual designs. Keyword search misses intent, and general vision-language models trained on natural images fit text-heavy infographics poorly. The new framework aligns user queries with design intent more closely, easing creation for newcomers.
arxiv-2604-08089: Liu and five colleagues propose GALA, a multimodal graph alignment framework for bug localization in program repair. Language-model repair tools perform well on textual benchmarks but struggle when bugs arrive with screenshots. Existing methods convert images into plain text, discarding spatial relationships and reducing finding to keyword matching. GALA shifts the task from implicit semantic guessing to structural reasoning. It first builds an Image UI Graph capturing visual elements and structural links, then aligns files by cross-checking the UI graph with repo structure to pinpoint faulty code.
arxiv-2604-08289: Kotov and Ciccarelli analyze error in image coding with quantization plus Hadamard transforms. The coding process has four steps: transform, quantize, inverse-quantize, and inverse-transform, using Hadamard transforms with a dead-zone quantizer. The aim is a theoretical tool for analyzing this process. They discuss error bounds and the largest absolute value result components can attain. To obtain these bounds, they use linear algebra methods and properties of Hadamard matrices. The resulting formulae depend on matrix size and quantizer and dequantizer settings.
arxiv-2604-08489: Magnan and Latter, in the second part of their vortex study, test whether the streaming instability can operate inside dust laden vortices. Reusing their dusty vortex models as backgrounds, they build a shearing box analogue that follows vortex streamlines and study short wavelength disturbances. Inertial and dust density waves prove non sinusoidal, yet a close cousin of the streaming instability stays active, strengthening the vortex route to planetesimals within stated limits.
arxiv-2604-08889: Osvaldo Angtuncio and Peralta extend matrix representations for scale functions of spectrally negative Lévy processes with rational jumps. The q scale function, from its Laplace transform, serves fluctuation theory, exit problems, hitting odds, ruin theory, and control. Ivanovs covered phase type jumps, but his Markov Brownian embedding cannot handle matrix exponential generality. Embedding the process into a fluid process modulated by a rational arrival process yields iterative schemes and a simple explicit scale function formula. It matches Ivanovs on phase type cases and shows orbit forms reach beyond them.
arxiv-2604-08989: Erram, Chouhan, and Tulapurkar investigate orbital angular momentum as a carrier of information in solids, beyond the usual spin channel used in orbitronics. Using two-port scattering measurements on ruthenium-nickel, ruthenium-platinum-cobalt-iron-boron, and cobalt-copper-silicon-dioxide devices, they probe orbital torque-driven motion and orbital pumping within the same platform. Their transmission data satisfy the symmetry relations demanded by Onsager reciprocity. This establishes orbital pumping as the reciprocal partner of orbital torque and unifies charge, orbital, and spin transport in one framework.
arxiv-2604-09089: Huang and eight colleagues diagnose a final-layer bottleneck in code-model security hardening. Final-layer supervision is common, yet vulnerability cues spread across layers and fade near outputs. Probing shows signals peak in intermediate-to-upper layers and fade toward the final layers. DeepGuard aggregates upper-layer representations through attention for a security analyzer balancing security and correctness, plus lightweight steering. Tests on five code models show secure-and-correct generation up 11.9 percent on average over baselines and generalization to unseen vulnerability types.
arxiv-2604-09189: Mittal audits whether language models follow their own safety rules, learned from feedback but never formally specified. Existing benchmarks test external standards, not whether models enforce their own stated boundaries. The Symbolic-Neural Consistency Audit extracts self-stated rules via prompts and formalizes them as typed predicates. Findings show absolute-refusal models frequently comply with harmful prompts, while reasoning models lead on consistency yet miss policies for 29 percent of categories. Cross-model agreement on rule types is low at 11 percent, showing a measurable, architecture-dependent say-do gap.
arxiv-2604-09289: Dwivedi, Sigovan, and Sixou propose a hybrid framework for parametric linear PDEs. A meta-learned predictor called KAPI maps coordinates and parameters to solution values while generating an adaptive Gaussian basis shape. A lightweight meta-network maps parameters to basis centers, widths, and activity patterns, learning how the basis space adapts across the family. That geometry feeds a corrector that adds a background basis and solves by one-shot least squares, often improving accuracy by orders of magnitude.
arxiv-2604-09389: Wiegand and colleagues ask whether more data is worth the cost, studying dataset scaling in a tiny attention-only decoder. Training transformer models is expensive, as performance improves with dataset size and budget, but small-scale implications remain less explored. They isolate dataset-size effects with a strongly reduced attention-only decoder, training on progressively larger power-of-two subsets. They observe smooth improvements with clear diminishing returns, and about 30 percent of data suffices for approximately 90 percent of full-data validation accuracy.
arxiv-2604-10289: Agca and Tekin show one scalar from membrane pressure reorganizing the familiar surfaces of a Kerr-Newman black hole. Its zeros sit at the outer and inner horizons, its poles at the stationary-limit surfaces, and its divergence carries the ring-singularity factor. Its large-distance behavior records the scalar decay. The construction is a compact diagnostic, not a new invariant characterization nor an extension of the membrane fluid into the interior. A secondary algebraic analogy links it to van der Waals equations of state.
arxiv-2604-10589: de los Riscos, Corbacho, and Arbib build a layered category-theory framework for schema-based learning, where knowledge is organized as reusable schemas. Four linked levels run from syntactic schemas through implemented versions to probabilistic models and semantic grounding. At the agent level, a duoidal structure supports schema workflows over mental objects, including memory and cognitive modules. Memory itself gets a categorical treatment with subsystems, data stores, and read-write operations. Higher levels place the agent in an architecture category and model multi-agent interaction with the world.
arxiv-2604-10789: Dong and six colleagues propose ReplicateAnyScene, a tool turning casual videos into compositional 3D scenes without manual prompting or extra visual inputs. A five-stage cascade extracts and aligns generic priors from vision models across textual, visual, and spatial dimensions, grounding them into structured 3D scenes that stay coherent and physically plausible. To test the task more fully, they introduce the C3DR benchmark for reconstruction quality from diverse angles. Tests show the method beats existing baselines in generating high-quality compositional 3D scenes.
arxiv-2604-11089: Lee and five colleagues introduce structured state-space regularization for compact image tokenization. Image tokenizers are central to generative models, where latent structure determines generation quality. A key new property is spectral order, encoding information across frequency parts. The authors derive an objective by revisiting state-space models as systems mimicking basis behaviour. Hidden states thus capture wave parts, yielding a rule giving spectral order in latent spaces. Tests show it improves model scores of them with only minimal rebuild loss.
arxiv-2604-11289: Maden and three colleagues monitor finite-time quantum heat engines with topology instead of energy readings alone. Weak measurements are embedded in time-delay form and mapped to persistent homology diagrams. A quality index built from Wasserstein and bottleneck distances tracks control decay and warns of cycle failure. Across noise settings from timing jitter to coherence injection, the topological monitor stays robust where a standard statistical baseline degrades. It also captures microscopic traces of quantum friction.
arxiv-2604-11389: Ghaffar Nia and six colleagues classify standard cine cardiac MRI views with ConvFormer3D-TAP. The model joins 3D convolutional tokens with multiscale self-attention. It is trained with masked space-time rebuilding and uncertainty-weighted clip fusion, which helps it handle phase variation and ambiguous segments. On 150,974 clinic cine sequences across six standard views, it reached 96 percent validation accuracy with per-class F1 scores at or above 0.94 and strong calibration. Remaining errors cluster in neighboring long-axis and outflow view pairs, reflecting prescription overlap.
arxiv-2604-11789: Yuan and nine colleagues review how large multimodal models meet object-centric vision, where scenes are handled as explicit objects rather than whole images. They organise recent work into four themes: object-centred understanding, referring segmentation, visual editing, and visual generation, and summarise the modelling styles, learning strategies, and evaluation methods behind them. Open problems include keeping object identity stable, fine spatial control, and reliable testing under shifted data.
arxiv-2604-12089: Bonaiti, Hagen, and Papenbrock study spatiotemporal patterns of density fluctuations in oxygen-16, oxygen-24, and calcium-48, using nuclear interactions from chiral effective field theory and the time-dependent coupled-cluster method. They find two-particle-two-hole excitations generate small-amplitude fluctuations that are fast, short-ranged, and stochastic in character. In this picture, two particles are excited out of their shells, leaving two holes behind.
arxiv-2604-12189: He and three colleagues show strong lensing of fast radio bursts can probe collapsed dark matter halos that challenge standard cosmology. Core-collapsed self-interacting halos have steeper central profiles than cold dark matter halos, widening the lensing cross section and stretching image time delays. Future all-sky monitors expected to catch 100,000 to 10 million bursts per decade could measure delay distributions well enough to probe self-interaction strengths.
arxiv-2604-12289: Tonneau and nine colleagues audit hate speech moderation on Twitter using 540,000 tweets from a full day, annotated by trained native speakers. Five months after posting, 80 percent of hateful tweets, including violent ones, stayed online, with removal barely likelier than for non-hateful posts and unmoved by severity and reach. Automated detection ranked hate highly but classified it unreliably, enabling human triage. Current staffing curbed little exposure, yet large cuts proved financially feasible, far below regulatory fines.
arxiv-2604-12389: Zhe Zhang and two colleagues release VoxEffects, a dataset of speech with exact effect records. Each item pairs produced speech with the effects applied and their settings. The benchmark asks models to detect effects, name presets, and predict strength. Degradations from recording gear and platforms test robustness. An AudioMAE multi-task baseline accompanies the release. Studies of domain shift, duration, and gender fairness are included.
arxiv-2604-12589: J. M. Mazón and J. Toledo study doubly nonlinear diffusion on metric graphs. Such graphs model complex tubular networks with axial diffusion as focus. Solutions exist and are unique for a very general class. Porous Medium and p-Laplacian evolution cases are covered. Diffusion may also change from edge to edge, reflecting tubule properties. Mixed Neumann-Kirchhoff rules apply at graph vertices. Tubes meet at joints. The work is pure math.
arxiv-2604-12689: Fabrizio Caragiulo and two colleagues study Cahn-Hilliard models with fractional derivatives. Higher-order derivatives replace standard ones, shaped by a wavy factor. Three regimes emerge from oscillation scale versus interface length. Convergence to a sharp-interface limit is proved in each regime. Extreme regimes show a separation effect. That marks the difference from local models. The work thus maps nonlocal limits across scales.
arxiv-2604-12889: Yuhao Huang and eight colleagues scale 3D photonic circuits to wafer size with reliable cavities. Two barriers block the way: taper efficiency versus footprint, and uneven loss across wafers. Etch-back assisted polishing evens the spacer layer across the wafer. A kappa-engineered taper lifts a reliability metric 75 percent above linear tapers. Two nitride layers show losses of 0.077 and 0.068 decibels per centimeter, with transition loss as low as 6 millidecibels. Low transition loss enables the first 3D high-Q cavities spanning two layers.
arxiv-2604-13089: Shnirelman maps the asymptotic spaces of the Lobachevsky plane, the structure of an unbounded metric space viewed at infinity. The full idea uses nonstandard analysis, and the given space depends on the chosen nonstandard extension of the standard universe. His complete treatment shows the Lobachevsky plane's asymptotic space is an R-tree, yet many distinct non-isometric spaces of this kind exist, with spaces of high cardinality.
arxiv-2604-13289: Kebande builds a cryptanalysis tool that pairs string-pattern checks with machine learning to probe stream-cipher keystreams. His Neural Stringology method pulls out repeated substrings, frequency patterns, and position stats tied to Add-Rotate-XOR steps. A neural model then hunts for breaks from randomness in those features. On the EChaCha20 cipher, including reduced-round versions, it picks out clear structure under controlled conditions.
arxiv-2604-13389: Haolin Zhang and four colleagues propose RoTE, a plug-in time embedding for sequential recommendation. Existing models sort interactions by time stamp but ignore the actual gaps between them, blurring how tastes shift over short and long spans. RoTE splits each time stamp into coarse and fine parts and adds those time parts to item codes, letting models sense time gaps with no backbone change. Applied to several Transformer recommenders on three benchmarks, it improves NDCG at five by up to about 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-13489: Flynn presents a unified corpus of 8,963 HI rotation curve measurements across 423 galaxies, with 438 total entries, 15 of them metadata-only THINGS galaxies. Drawn from SPARC, THINGS, LITTLE THINGS, and WALLABY DR2, the corpus ships as a single structured JSON file holding nested per-ring kinematic data, survey metadata, column definitions, and quality annotations. It also includes a 438-row flat CSV for catalog filtering. A two-tier quality system separates hand-curated curves with per-point uncertainties from automated pipeline products. Three worked examples each need fewer than 15 lines of Python.
arxiv-2604-13589: Chen and Wang remove smoke from multi-view footage and then rebuild the scene in three dimensions, a pipeline built for a 2026 restoration challenge. First, a generative tool cleans each frame and brightness is normalized; then 3D Gaussian Splatting is trained with physics-based helpers for depth, dark-channel, and gradient consistency. On the Akikaze validation scene the result reaches 20.98 decibels, beating the unregularized baseline.
arxiv-2604-13689: Zulawinski and Wylomanska build tools for time series that repeat in cycles, with wild spikes and infinite variance. Tools assume tame data, but these series break that rule. The goal is tools that stay honest when spikes dominate. Their fractional lower-order covariance replaces the ordinary version. From it come two new measures, peFLOACF and peFLOPACF, extending the classic periodic tools. The measures support a dependence test and a way to choose model order for periodic autoregressive and moving-average models. Simulations and air pollution data confirm they work.
arxiv-2604-13789: Yoo and four colleagues track a single object in 3D LiDAR sequences with ChronoTrack, a long-term memory framework. Earlier memory methods use only a few recent frames, limited by temporal feature inconsistency and memory overhead. ChronoTrack keeps a compact set of learnable memory tokens and enforces two consistencies: feature alignment across frames over time, and diverse token representations via memory-point-memory cyclic walks. The result leads multiple 3D tracking benchmarks while running at 42 frames per second on one RTX 4090 card.
arxiv-2604-14189: Wang and Alkhalifah present SWEEP, a unified solver library for modeling seismic wavefields and running inversions. It supports acoustic, elastic, attenuative, VTI, and TTI engines plus their Born approximations. Built-in automatic differentiation enables full-waveform inversion, least-squares reverse-time migration, and other gradient methods. A plug-and-play design lets users combine custom losses, multi-GPU runs, and neural networks with ease, making SWEEP a flexible platform for advanced seismic inverse problems.
arxiv-2604-14489: Singaravadivelan, Gupta, Wang, and MacLellan present CobwebTM, a low-parameter hierarchical topic model that learns over time from streaming text without preset topic counts. Neural topic models need heavy tuning and forget under streaming data, while classical probabilistic models lack flexibility, so the team adapts Cobweb to continuous document embeddings. CobwebTM builds semantic hierarchies online, finding topics, creating new ones on the fly, and organizing them in layers. Across varied data sets it shows strong coherence, topics that hold steady over time, and high-quality hierarchies.
arxiv-2604-15389: Wayo and three colleagues build a hardware-to-decoder stack for hybrid continuous- and discrete-variable quantum error correction in LiDMaS+. Provider records normalize into one decoder contract and replay under fixed controls across four decoders, with perfect replay integrity on fixtures and real slices. Decoder choice proves regime-dependent: belief propagation cuts correction volume about 49 percent on fixtures and about 50 percent on real data versus MWPM.
arxiv-2604-15489: Hosseinzadeh and nine colleagues propose QQMR, a Q-learning multipath routing method for wireless body-area networks in the Internet of Medical Things. Data splits into three priority levels with tiered queues that adapt and fuzzy C-means grouping, and each data type keeps its own learning policy for primary and backup paths. Tests show better packet delivery with lower delay, routing overhead, and energy use than existing methods.
arxiv-2604-15789: Si, Li, Backes, and Zhang take stock of no-training trust fixes for LLMs. These fixes are judged all over the map, cover few trust sides, and can dent skill or add snap-back. The team re-tests top no-training fixes at three cut points, input, guts, and output, across LLM lines and sizes, weighing trust, skill, toughness, and cost. Their read lays out swaps and open knots and hands out hands-on tips for poising trust, skill, and toughness with no extra training.
arxiv-2604-15989: Ivanov and Antonov compute charged-current quasi-elastic neutrino and antineutrino scattering cross sections on carbon-12. They use the coherent density fluctuation model with an effective nucleon mass set at 0.8 times the free nucleon mass, plus two-particle emission. Predictions cover cross sections observed at MiniBooNE, T2K, and MINERvA. They also analyze the axial form factor for Delta excitation at zero momentum transfer, important for meson-exchange currents, and test results across momentum regions.
arxiv-2604-16089: Combe and Nencka present a shape frame for rebuild problems based on Vaisman foliations and Atiyah-Molino chains. Free maps induce cross links and dual links; zero torsion and bend duality ensure unique, path-free results, while blocks yield non-associative quasigroupoids. Toric balance gives one answer. Uses in generative AI filling and cryo-electron imaging show the frame's real power, joining shape math with data-driven inverse problems.
arxiv-2604-16189: Schöllkopf and 18 colleagues report a two-colour, dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser at the Fritz Haber Institute, adding a far-infrared beamline to the existing mid-infrared machine. A 500 megahertz kicker cavity splits the electron bunch train so one stream feeds each laser, letting both run together in sync. Each laser's wavelength can be tuned independently over a wide range, up to a factor of four, by varying undulator gaps.
arxiv-2604-16489: Zhao, Huang, Fu and Hao address the unit commitment problem at the heart of power system operation, where specialized solvers are tightly tied to single variants and fail on others. Their method decouples solver from problem by reducing every variant uniformly to SAT instances that standard SAT solvers can handle. One algorithm can then solve many variants, rather than each variant needing its own. Experiments showed better solution quality than specialized algorithms and stronger generalizability, offering a fast, flexible framework for new formulations as power systems evolve.
arxiv-2604-16789: The ATLAS Collaboration searches for massive long-lived particles decaying into displaced vertices at the LHC. Such particles travel into the detector before decaying into multiple visible tracks. A Run 2 search covers displaced vertices in events triggered by missing energy, and a Run 3 search covers those triggered by muons. The Run 2 search first uses a fuzzy vertex reconstruction algorithm alongside the standard one, setting limits on Higgs Portal, SUSY and DFSZ axino models. The Run 3 search first uses a displaced muon trigger, setting limits on RPV SUSY models.
arxiv-2604-16989: Balko and seven colleagues report eight new results in mathematics and theoretical computer science produced with Bolzano, an open-source multi-agent language-model system. Bolzano runs rounds of interaction between parallel prover agents and a verifier agent, carrying a shared knowledge base across rounds. Six results reach publishable quality, five were produced essentially on their own by the system, and the work suggests language models can contribute meaningfully to math research.
arxiv-2604-17089: Cho and three colleagues build Tree of Concepts, an interpretable continual-learning framework for shifting clinical data. A shallow decision tree defines a fixed rule-based concept interface, while a concept bottleneck model predicts those concepts from raw features. Updates touch only the concept extractor and label head, so concept meanings and explanations stay steady over time, beating replay-enhanced baselines on tabular healthcare benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-17189: Tsunoda, Goto, and Sato propose a sheepdog control method for drone swarms that predicts swarm behavior while respecting robots' motion limits. A few navigator agents steer many autonomous agents toward a target, but past guidance laws treated both as point masses driven by interaction vectors. Their 3D law, inspired by the Dynamic Window Approach, generates feasible motion candidates at each control cycle and predicts short-term swarm evolution with an internal model. Candidates are scored on target progress, swarm positioning, and safety margins. Numerical simulations confirm safe, efficient guidance.
arxiv-2604-17289: Ghiasvand, Beliaev, Alizadeh, and Pedarsani tackle noisy crowd labels in language-model training. Standard vote-counting lets careless annotators corrupt the model. Their method REALM learns a reliability score for each annotator alongside the model itself. Each label is treated as a mix of the model's guess and random chance. It topped rivals on real crowdsourced text tasks and beat plain noisy training in 152 of 162 question-answering setups.
arxiv-2604-17589: Zhang presents a pointwise bound, basic in form, for the irreducible characters of SU(3), and derives new Lp bounds for these characters as an application. The approach rests on how characters descend to singular sets and on cancellation in the resulting formula. The paper offers a concise representation-theoretic result, giving a concrete pointwise estimate plus improved integrability bounds for SU(3) characters.
arxiv-2604-18289: Thakur and six colleagues estimate the relative states of drone swarms from event-camera views of spinning propellers. Frame cameras are slow and fail in harsh light, while event cameras offer low latency and microsecond timing. The system tracks propellers in the event stream, turns per-propeller frequencies into thrust inputs, and fits ellipses to recover tilt. On five real outdoor flights, propeller frequency error stays under 3 percent, enabling decentralized localization for multi-robot teams.
arxiv-2604-18489: Meng and four colleagues align language models for lyric-to-melody writing with rule-based musical constraints. Plain tuning alone yields off tunes with poor rhythm and wrong vocal ranges, a flaw the authors call constraint violation. Their system writes musical rules, auto-builds a liking data set from tuned-model outputs, and aligns in two stages: direct preference optimization on pairs, then Kahneman-Tversky optimization on single bad cases. The aligned model cuts rule breaks and beats strong rivals on measured and listener tests.
arxiv-2604-18589: Wang, Huang, and Dragut present CentaurTA Studio, a web system for self-improving human-agent teamwork in open coding and theme construction. It joins two-stage feedback splitting mock drafting and expert checks, prompt tuning turning feedback into rules, and rubric-based scoring with early stopping. Across three domains, it leads open coding and theme building, reaching 92.12 percent and beating rivals. Without the feedback loop, scores drop from 90 percent to 81 percent. The full system peaks within 10 rounds, about 25 minutes, boosting speed over expert polish.
arxiv-2604-18789: Liang and seven colleagues present ARES, a framework that finds and repairs systemic weaknesses in reinforcement learning from human feedback, where both the core model and the reward model fail together. A Safety Mentor builds adversarial prompts from topics, personas, tactics, and goals, and generates malicious and safe responses to expose both at once. Repair proceeds in two stages: first tuning the reward model to detect harmful content better, then using it to optimize the core model. Across safety benchmarks, ARES greatly improves safety while preserving capabilities.
arxiv-2604-18989: Liu, Shi, and Zhang prove Anderson localization for the hierarchical Anderson-Bernoulli model on lattices of any dimension. It pairs a layered structure with random independent Bernoulli draws. In this setting, waves stay trapped rather than spreading freely through the lattice. Their method also yields a likely unique continuation result on integer lattices.
arxiv-2604-19089: Jung, Lee, and Lim propose LightEdit for scalable lifelong knowledge editing in language models. Models need frequent updates for changing facts, but parameter edits destabilize later edits through forgetting, while retrieval methods cost too much across data sets. LightEdit first picks relevant knowledge from retrieved information to reshape the query, then damps original knowledge odds during decoding. Tests on ZSRE, Counterfact, and RIPE show it beats current lifelong editing methods. By cutting training costs, it adapts easily across data sets.
arxiv-2604-19489: Achmann-Denkler, Haim, and Wolff evaluate two model kinds for visual political communication analysis on Instagram: specialized machine learning models and multimodal large language models. They focus on concentrated visibility in stories and posts during the 2021 German federal election campaign. They compare traditional computer vision models with GPT-4o at spotting leading politicians and tallying people in images. GPT-4o outperforms the other models, with strong macro F1-scores for face recognition and person counting in stories. This shows advanced AI systems can scale visual content analysis.
arxiv-2604-19689: Wang and eight colleagues present A-MAR, an agent-based tool that retrieves evidence for artwork questions by following a structured reasoning plan. Given a work and a query, the tool first breaks the task into steps. Each step states its goal and what evidence it needs, and the tool then searches only for that targeted material. The step-by-step answers, each tied to its sources, are meant to be easier to check than the hidden reasoning of large multimodal models, which rely on stored knowledge alone.
arxiv-2604-19789: Alfred and Sundararaghavan present an autonomous language model agent for end-to-end, data-driven materials theory development. The agent picks an equation form, generates and runs its own code, and tests how well the theory matches the data without human help. It combines step-by-step reasoning with expert-supplied tools, adjusting its approach when required while keeping a clear record of its decisions. For established cases like the Hall-Petch equation and Paris law, it correctly identifies the governing equation and predicts reliably on new datasets.
arxiv-2604-19889: Lóio, De Nardis, and Jin model quantum dynamics with negative Markov chains, a particle-antiparticle sampling picture. In this picture, complexity grows as random particles multiply, until classical sampling fails. They prove that for unitaries built from local or pairwise parts, some noise channel always curbs that growth. An open spin chain under depolarizing noise then crosses an exact, computable threshold into classical simulability once noise tops a critical level.
arxiv-2604-19989: Flynn, Ivanov, and Yazici propose an online edge-mapping method for synthetic aperture radar on small drones. Classic radar processing stores back-scattered signals and rebuilds images later, burdening limited onboard memory. Their direct method skips image reconstruction and classifies scenes and targets from edge maps instead. Edge maps are naturally sparse, so the approach needs fewer measurements and less computing power than backprojection-style reconstruction.
arxiv-2604-20089: Fulop and Gershenfeld show that field-driven effects, from flash sintering to electromigration, share one key onset voltage. Threshold fields span six orders of size, yet their product with the onset coherence length always lands between about a tenth of a volt and under three volts. That voltage is the work needed to link in tune with the phonon damping peak, where lattice softening peaks. The same rule joins large-scale heat-driven breakdowns with the tiny-scale Blech limit, covering 17 crystal types.
arxiv-2604-20189: Le and Doan give new bounds on Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves, beating Lvovsky's 1996 bound under conditions. A monomial curve comes from coprime integers zero to top value d, with gaps as spaces between neighbors minus one. The 1983 Gruson-Lazarsfeld-Peskine bound caps regularity at d minus k plus two, the full gap sum plus two. Lvovsky showed two biggest gaps plus two suffice. New bounds rest on Apéry sets and Frobenius numbers, yield Cohen-Macaulay and Buchsbaum tests, and come with algorithms and sumset use.
arxiv-2604-20589: Christoph, Diskin, Lichev, and Sudakov study edge-expansion in random 0/1 polytopes. They prove the graph of a random polytope, with each vertex kept with probability p, has edge-expansion on the order of d. That holds with high probability for p up to 1 minus epsilon. That improves the previous bound and verifies the Mihail-Vazirani conjecture for random 0/1 polytopes. Behavior changes at p equals 1/2. For p at most 1/2 minus epsilon, the graph has edge-expansion at least on the order of d to the k for every k.
arxiv-2604-21189: Meg Wilkinson and five colleagues keep a 7-jointed robot arm safe in changing rooms with a single smooth safety function built from Poisson's equation. Sampling the arm's surface and shrinking free space by a safety margin yields one function for the whole scene, enforced by a real-time filter. They prove that guarding the sampled points guards the entire continuous arm surface, and validate the scheme on a 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator.
arxiv-2604-21589: Licheng Zhang and two colleagues strengthen Turán bounds for 1-planar graphs. Bekos and colleagues proved every triangle-free 1-planar graph on 4 or more vertices has at most 3n - 6 edges. They strengthen this bound to 3n - 8, tight for even n at least 8. Every K4-free 1-planar graph on 3 or more vertices has at most floor of 7n/2 - 7 edges, tight for n at least 9. Every K5-free 1-planar graph on 3 or more vertices has at most 4n - 8 edges, tight for n = 8 and n at least 10.
arxiv-2604-22089: Tan, Wang, and Li coin ethics testing, a way to build tests that systematically catch harm in text, code, or images made automatically by generative AI. Unlike fairness testing, which hunts bias, ethics testing looks for harm from unethical behavior, such as harmful acts or breaches of intellectual property rights. The authors lay out the idea, name its challenges, and run five case studies showing how ethics testing works for generative AI systems.
arxiv-2604-22189: Raxit and six colleagues present an energy-efficient multi-robot coverage framework for large nonconvex regions with obstacles and no-fly zones. MRCPP generates globally-informed swaths and parallel sweeping paths with minimal turns. It adds safety buffers and an mTSP solver balancing workloads and mission time. A modified visibility graph connects disjoint segments while tracking heading angles. Real-world tests with aerial and surface vehicles show MRCPP beating top planners. It cuts average energy use by 3 to 40 percent for 3 robots and computation time by an order of magnitude.
arxiv-2604-22389: Samokhin studies spreading shock waves in spherical and cylindrical KdV-B equations, equations with few known exact solutions that are hard to interpret. He gives a detailed account of long-term shape for one-parameter sets of shock wave solutions. He proves their stability using a conservation law. From those results he derives rules for superposition. Those rules apply to a wide class of shock waves, including broken ones. Typical examples are shown with graphs.
arxiv-2604-23289: Totakura and Chakraborty build MetaErr, a meta-model that predicts whether a base deep neural network succeeds or fails on a given sample. Observing the base model's performance on a learning task, it forecasts failure in advance, a problem far less studied than cutting error rates. The meta-model ignores the base model's architecture and training parameters entirely, staying agnostic to its design. Tests on three computer vision benchmarks beat strong baselines, and the framework also improves pseudo-label-based semi-supervised learning.
arxiv-2604-23389: Layden, Dey, and Coley give a full invariant description of the Kerr spacetime, the rotating black-hole solution, and use it to pin down its photon region. They build a function whose zeros pick out light paths that graze every photon surface, and show one parameter, acting like an inclination angle, labels all spherical photon orbits. The same invariants also identify surfaces such as ergosurfaces and local horizons.
arxiv-2604-23589: Fazili and Jyothi propose XITE, a data-augmentation trick for cross-lingual transfer in multilingual language models. Starting from unlabelled text in a low-resource language, it borrows the label of a similar English example, then blends the two embeddings to create synthetic training data. First moving the target text into a rich-language subspace boosts results further, with large gains for sentiment analysis and even larger ones for inference tasks.
arxiv-2604-23689: Glozman reviews the high-temperature QCD phase diagram at small chemical potentials, where three regimes differ in symmetries, degrees of freedom, and scaling with the number of colours. Below the chiral restoration temperature lies a hadron gas, between that and deconfinement lies a stringy fluid, and above deconfinement lies the quark-gluon plasma. The review surveys recent developments across all three regimes.
arxiv-2604-23789: Zhang and seven colleagues introduce MuSS, a large dataset and benchmark for multi-shot subject-to-video generation drawn from over 3,000 movies. A progressive captioning pipeline secures shot-level accuracy before global story coherence. Cross-shot matching kills the copy-paste shortcut of reusing the subject image. Tests show current baselines falter on story logic or degenerate into sticker generators. A MuSS-trained model leads on story and identity preservation.
arxiv-2604-23989: Tanaka and Sato analyze Scattered Forest Search, a tree-search method for fixing programs across several turns, through the lens of version spaces from learning theory. They introduce a depth-first refiner and a width-first refiner that fixes starting programs while improving repair instructions, then place the full method between the two. The analysis finds it behaves closer to the instruction refiner, suggesting the simpler method may match it with less machinery.
arxiv-2604-24089: Shahane and five colleagues present BiMol-Diff, a single diffusion framework for both molecule generation from text and molecule captioning. Standard diffusion corrupts all positions alike, which can damage structurally key tokens, while autoregressive models strain on long-range links. A token-aware noise schedule corrupts each position by how hard it is to recover, protecting tough substructures. On ChEBI-20 and M3-20M it gains about 15 percent in exact match for reconstruction and leads baselines on captioning scores.
arxiv-2604-24189: Loosveldt, Nachit, and Nourdin study stochastic differential equations driven by finite-order chaos processes on Wiener spaces. The noise comes from fixed-order Wiener-Itô integrals, giving non-Gaussian motion. Under mild assumptions they prove solutions exist and are unique, then prove Malliavin differentiability and absolute continuity of the solution law. Without the usual Gaussian setting, they use the Kusuoka-Stroock approach, and density results follow under ellipticity, independence, and non-degeneracy.
arxiv-2604-24289: Chinesta, Falco, and Falco-Pomares study unit-range integration by quantum amplitude estimation, focusing on oracle cost. They define functions with bounded angle maps, checkable in fast-growing time with a Walsh-Hadamard transform. Each function has an encoding circuit with multi-gated turns. Circuit bounds plus errors give a depth-accuracy trade-off for smooth functions. Encoding degree and Sobolev smoothness stand apart, and tests on Triangulum and Kingston confirm the pattern. Affine codes run on both, while square codes exceed Triangulum time limit but run on Kingston.
arxiv-2604-24589: Ren, Guo, Zuo and Zhang build AstroVLBench, a benchmark of over 4,100 expert-checked tasks testing vision-language models on real astronomical data across imaging, radio interferometry, photometry, light curves and spectroscopy. Six leading models show strongly modality-dependent performance and trail specialized methods, though one model leads most consistently. Physical explanations in prompts beat purely descriptive hints, and giving models raw numerical tables instead of plots improves scores by up to 13 percentage points.
arxiv-2604-24889: Liu and six colleagues map the phase diagram of a dual-species Rydberg ladder in one dimension. They use large-scale density-matrix renormalization group calculations. They find disordered phases and ordered phases with Z2, Z3 and Z4 symmetry. They also find floating phases with incommensurate wave vectors and slowly decaying correlations. A smooth crossover links distinct Z2-ordered regimes, reflecting reorganization of low-energy states rather than a true transition. They also find a multi-critical point where Ising, chiral and first-order lines meet.
arxiv-2604-25389: Bodei and three colleagues study how students weave AI into academic writing. Study 1 surveys 107 UK students on AI use across five stages: ideas, sourcing, planning, drafting, and review. It links use to AI skill, trust, confidence, authorship worries, and drive. Study 2 interviews 12 postgraduates about marked writing habits. Together, the studies find AI use is picky and varied. It falls into three value-led shapes: early-stage learning help, late-stage quality help, and side-line productivity help. The work shows how students juggle learning, quality, speed, and authorship.
arxiv-2604-25989: Bas i Beneito, Palavrić, and Sainaghi build an effective field theory framework for events that change baryon number by two units. They construct the complete minimal set of low-energy terms from chiral symmetry. The set is linked to Standard Model theory and baryon chiral perturbation theory. Applied to baryon-antibaryon oscillations and dinucleon decay, the framework shows oscillations probing only a narrow subset of term structures. Dinucleon decay reaches a much broader class, including new untried channels that can probe open value ranges.
arxiv-2604-26089: Bar and thirteen colleagues show that domain shape, not thickness or edge effects, decides whether free-standing barium titanate membranes switch sharply or smoothly. Thick membranes with large single-domain regions display clear latent heat. Thinner membranes packed with dense domains switch smoothly, despite the same shape change shown by diffraction. Imaging links this to domain-size change. A Ginzburg-Landau analysis shows smaller domains cutting the free-energy barrier. The result points to domain design as a route to stronger caloric effects.
arxiv-2604-26189: Bürger and four colleagues study how porous Bravais lattice unit-cells settle in viscous fluid, varying pore share at will through lattice spacing. Tests in a tank find sinking speed fits a power law in solid fraction with the same power for all cell shapes. Analysis and models show tank walls shaping that power; fixing for wall effects with a Faxen boundary term gives a lower power for open settling. That helps estimate sedimentation fluxes of complex objects in clouds and oceans, though irregular natural aggregates remain open.
arxiv-2604-26389: Dev and nineteen colleagues measured how neutral hydrogen gas relates to dark matter halo mass, combining DINGO pilot data with GAMA spectra and WAVES photometry. Direct detections plus spectral stacking traced halo gas across a wide mass range, and adding photometric members recovered satellite gas past spectroscopic limits. The relation follows a double power law with a turnover at intermediate masses, centrals ruling below it and satellites above. Photometric members raised measured gas in massive halos by a factor of one and a half to three.
arxiv-2604-26489: Wang and three colleagues examined deep networks inside feature-interaction recommenders through the lens of dimensional collapse. Some work credits deep nets with capturing high-order interactions implicitly, while other work doubts they even learn second-order dot products well. Testing parallel and stacked networks across two models, the authors found both forms mitigate embedding collapse. A gradient-based theoretical analysis, backed by experiments, uncovered the mechanisms behind that collapse.
arxiv-2604-26789: Cepila, Goncalves, and Ridzikova investigate sub-nucleon shifts in deeply virtual Compton scattering at the EIC for proton and nuclear targets. Under the hot-spot model, they estimate energy patterns of coherent and incoherent cross sections across settings and atomic numbers, plus forecasts. Sub-nucleon shifts in the proton produce a turn-over in incoherent energy pattern, with the peak position set by virtuality. The coherent-to-incoherent ratio grows with energy and atomic number. It grows at smaller momentum transfer. Nuclear incoherent spread peaks at fixed beam energy.
arxiv-2604-26989: Kable, Mills and Wright show the subgroup formed by (2^n-1)-th powers is a cap set inside the field of order 2^{2n}. Two cases illustrate it, each tied to a card game and each maximal. One is the 20 nonzero fourth powers, taken in the field of order 81, the SET case. The other is, in the field of order 64, the 9 nonzero seventh powers, the EvenQuads case. Cosets of these subgroups split their fields' multiplicative groups into maximal caps. Certain multiplicative subgroups of the fields of orders 243 and 729 are also cap sets.
arxiv-2604-27089: Gupta and five colleagues introduce AutoSP, the first automated tool for long-context language-model training. Current libraries lack easy long-context abstractions, forcing users to rewrite code to compose sequence parallelism and other optimizations, a job needing deep expertise. AutoSP compiles models and applies sequence parallelism plus long-context-aware checkpointing, lifting trainability at negligible throughput cost. On NVIDIA hardware it extends training contexts by up to nearly three times, and on AMD hardware by about two and a half times, over hand-written baselines.
arxiv-2604-27189: Schouten and de Leeuw provide a quantum group description for long-range changes of quantum integrable spin chains. Those chains are generated by local, boost, and bilocal operators. The changes were well understood at the level of charges that commute. But their quantum group structures had not been recognized. For uniform Yang-Baxter integrable spin chains to first order, the changes come from a twist of the underlying quantum group's algebra. That twisting yields a generally non-associative algebra with a non-trivial Drinfeld associator.
arxiv-2604-27289: McCann leads with the Governance Invariance Theorem: governance stays uniform across the tower, with level n plus 1 reducing to level n by sameness of type. The Coinductive Safety Predicate captures governance safety for endless behaviors through a boolean permit flag, provably false for ungoverned input-output and true for governed readings. Around those two, the paper presents five results on structural governance for cognitive workflow systems in total. Three are machine-checked in Coq 8.19 using Interaction Trees with parameter-based coinduction, while two are proved on paper with explicit steps.
arxiv-2604-27589: Jia and four colleagues propose a unified 5G-IoT framework using CAMARA open gateways and a federated SDN architecture. CAMARA gateways expose network capabilities through standardized, open APIs, cutting fragmentation and easing interoperability across public and private 5G networks and varied IoT networks. The federated SDN layer supplies scalable cross-domain control. The team also demos remote control of KNX devices over 5G, stretching industrial and building automation toward a secure, dynamic network of networks.
arxiv-2604-27789: Chishti, Oyinloye, and Li propose a deploy-side control framework for LLM updates, tackling silent vendor changes that cause drift. The framework rests on live contracts setting allowed behavior, risk-type testing suites, and fit gates blocking updates that fail safety and quality standards. Focused testing in risk areas uncovers slips that overall metrics miss, in early checks across several LLM versions. The paper names open gaps: building test suites, setting sound thresholds in random systems, and spotting and tracing drift with vendors hiding details.
arxiv-2604-28089: Liu and Yin propose a source-independent quantum key distribution protocol that closes source side-channel attacks without pre-sending entanglement. Unlike the standard prepare-and-measure approach, which stays vulnerable even with a perfect single-photon source, their scheme uses non-classical light to secure the source side. Theory shows it doubles transmission distance while tolerating source imperfections, giving practical security gains over conventional laser schemes.
arxiv-2605-00089:
Bruno Bucciotti, Paolo Creminelli, Alessandro Longo, Warin Patrick McBlain, and Enrico Trincherini study what superluminality can even mean in gravitational effective field theories. A healthy theory should not allow faster-than-light signals, but with gravity there is no fixed Minkowski light cone to compare against. Their criterion is asymptotic: can the theory make signals outrun what the spacetime's asymptotic structure allows?

They analyze signal propagation in black hole backgrounds with higher-derivative operators. In more than four dimensions, effective light cones can produce genuine asymptotic superluminality, which can bound the theory's validity. In four dimensions the asymptotic causal structure proves identical to Schwarzschild's: prompt light rays ignore the corrections, and no asymptotic time advance is possible for any such theory. They also discuss two ways to define superluminality in four dimensions.
arxiv-2605-00189:
Alberto Bressan, Laura Caravenna, and Wen Shen study what smoothed versions of conservation laws look like up close, right where the true solution breaks. Conservation laws govern quantities such as traffic density or gas flow, and their solutions can form shocks, sharp jumps in the state. Many approximation schemes exist, from added viscosity to numerical grids, and broad convergence results are known.

The open question is local: near a shock, a shock collision, or the birth of a new shock, what pattern does an approximation settle into? The authors argue that, after a careful rescaling of space and time near such a point, the approximations approach a specific eternal solution defined for all space and time. They give precise results in the vanishing viscosity case, the scheme where a small smoothing term fades away.
arxiv-2605-00289:
Gayathri Viswanath and 10 co-authors report spectroscopic monitoring of a young giant planet still gathering material, Delorme 1 (AB)b. The companion has about thirteen times Jupiter's mass and circles a pair of stars on a wide orbit. Helium emission lines can reveal how gas falls onto such an object, a view hydrogen lines do not fully give.

The team analyzed thirty-three high-resolution spectra from a major telescope in Chile. Seven helium lines stood out clearly, changing from visit to visit. Several lines split into a narrow part near rest and a broader part shifted toward the red, a shape like that seen in young accreting stars but narrower. The authors trace the narrow part to gas just after the accretion shock, near the planet's surface, and the broad part to the shock front itself.
arxiv-2605-00389:
Mohammad Raihanul Bashar and 3 co-authors add game design to a virtual reality trainer for ultrasound-guided catheter insertion. VR simulators are common in procedural medical training, but many chase realism while giving trainees little formative feedback along the way. The team's simulator answers practice attempts with aligned sights and sounds: progress indicators, guidance, and rewards.

Studies with twenty-four novices and twelve clinicians compared the gamified trainer in use. Gamification cut task time, improved usability scores, and lowered the workload trainees reported. Novices described clearer goals and greater confidence, while experienced clinicians said the pacing of their work improved. The authors conclude that game-style feedback can serve as effective formative feedback in VR medical training, not merely as decoration on top of it.
arxiv-2605-00589:
Taro Kimura and Sanchita Sharma study reflection symmetry for Dirac operators on a finite warped cylinder, a curved tube used as a clean model in spectral theory. Their operator is twisted by a complex line bundle whose holonomy, the phase picked up around the tube, is a parameter. Boundary conditions follow the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer rule, standard for such problems.

They prove the reflection lifts to a unitary symmetry of the twisted setting exactly when twice the holonomy parameter is an integer. In that matching case, reflection pairs up the angular modes, the paired boundary blocks match exactly, and its trace sits on the single self-paired zero-mode sector. They then let the setting vary. With fixed trivial holonomy the family keeps an O(2) equivariance, and its spectral flow splits into named parts. With varying holonomy that equivariance breaks, and only a parity sign survives.
arxiv-2605-00789:
Xihao Chen, Yangyang Guo, and Roger Zimmermann present LightKV, a way to shrink the key-value cache that large vision-language models keep during inference. The cache speeds decoding, but vision tokens from the prefill stage consume large amounts of GPU memory. LightKV reduces that load by exploiting redundancy among vision-token embeddings, guided by the text prompt.

Cross-modality message passing gathers useful information across vision tokens and compresses them step by step during prefill. In tests on eight open models and eight benchmarks, keeping only about half the vision tokens halved the vision cache and cut computation by up to forty percent. General performance held up, and LightKV beat existing baselines by a clear margin.
arxiv-2605-00989:
Yuval Grossman, Guglielmo Papiri, and Stefan Schacht study CP violation induced by neutral kaon mixing in a specific charm meson decay, D-zero to two neutral kaons. CP violation measures a fundamental asymmetry between matter and antimatter behavior. The question is whether kaon mixing, a well-known source, can contribute noticeably to the asymmetry expected in this decay channel.

The authors show the kaon mixing contribution arises only together with second-order weak interactions in the D decay. They estimate the effect at a very small level, negligible compared with current experimental sensitivity and with the expected contribution from CP violation in the charm sector itself. Similar reasoning, they note, can be applied to other systems where such mixing effects might be suspected.
arxiv-2605-01189:
Chandrasekaran and five co-authors present NEURON, a neuro-symbolic system for grounded clinical explainability in health forecasting models. Adoption in clinics is blocked because strong models act as black boxes without grounding in medical concepts or a clear account of their logic. NEURON joins structured data views based on the SNOMED CT medical ontology with machine learning models, bridging raw data and medical nomenclature.

A retrieval-augmented language model layer merges feature scores and per-patient notes into clear plain-language explanations. Tested on MIMIC-IV data for acute heart failure mortality forecasting, NEURON improves discrimination over the base range. It also greatly beats SHAP-based accounts on human-aligned metrics. The authors present the system as a scalable route to trusted connected health uses.
arxiv-2605-01489:
Tianshi Zheng and seven co-authors build research agents that can do frontier science, not just look facts up. Deep research agents learn by hunting information, but science problems hide in sparse, scattered papers and demand heavy computation, so graph-built or browsing-built training data fall short.

Their framework, SciResearcher, makes the training data itself: it synthesizes varied concept and computation tasks grounded in academic proof, and drills information hunting, tool use, and long chains of steps. Fine-tuning plus agentic reinforcement learning on that data yields SciResearcher-8B. At its size it sets a new mark on a hard biology and chemistry bench, beats several larger closed agents, and posts double-digit gains on hard graduate-level biology and literature test sets. The authors offer the pipeline as a scalable route to scientific agents.
arxiv-2605-01689:
Khalid Mahmud Labib, Saad Waheed, Bakhtiar Nafis, and Shabbir Ahmed watch a lithium-ion battery age by turning its dynamics into a network and reading the network's decay. Circuit stand-ins with fixed parts cannot follow the shifting chemistry inside a wearing cell, so the team work from operating data alone.

A control-aware mode decomposition first extracts the battery's modes from the data. The mode matrix becomes a weighted adjacency matrix, a graph whose nodes are dynamic states and whose links carry their coupling strength. Graph measures, connectivity and a modularity proxy among them, then track structure across aging stages. The healthy battery reads as one tight, coherent web. With wear, the web thins, fragments, and grows uneven. The authors offer the graph view as an interpretable gauge of system-level aging that no single voltage curve shows.
arxiv-2605-02389:
Joost Van Veen, Luise Prielinger, and Sebastian Feld improve reinforcement learning for routing circuits in distributed quantum systems. Scaling one quantum processor is hard, so qubits are spread across smaller linked modules. Compilation then means placing, routing, and using qubits across modules, with state-dependent choices about when and where to create shared remote states for remote operations.

Building on a 2024 framework by Promponas and colleagues, the authors introduce an agent with a new action-space formulation and effective action masking. Action-space engineering, shaping what moves the agent may choose, is their lever for faster, better policies. A broad numerical comparison tests the new approach against the earlier one across circuits.
arxiv-2605-02589:
Hedi Tabia and eight co-authors survey how machines learn useful representations from optical coherence tomography images of the retina. This scan type gives sharp, non-invasive views of retinal layers and is now central to eye care. Clinics produce huge volumes of scans, and automated reading promises less reliance on scarce expert labels and more consistent results across devices.

The survey organizes the field by learning style. Covered areas include supervised networks, self-supervised and semi-supervised methods, generative approaches, three-dimensional modeling, multimodal learning, and large pretrained foundation models, including vision-language systems. For each area the authors trace main contributions, note limits that persist, and follow links between older and newer work. The review serves as a map for researchers entering retinal image analysis.
arxiv-2605-02789:
Mario Rodríguez Béjar and two co-authors present FunFuzz, a fuzzing framework that uses language models to hunt compiler bugs. Fuzzing feeds a program crafted inputs to trigger faults, and model-written inputs can be well structured. But results swing with the starting prompt and random sampling, wasting effort on repeated inputs.

FunFuzz runs several isolated searches in parallel, like islands, and migrates strong candidates between them to keep variety. Starting prompts come from documentation, with topic-specific instructions per island, and prompts adapt under feedback as the run goes. Candidates are ranked by new compiler coverage, and compiler-internal failure signals flag crash inputs. In day-long campaigns on two major compilers, the framework reached higher coverage than prior model-driven baselines and found more distinct failures.
arxiv-2605-02889:
Roman Gorazd introduces gluing diagrams, a combinatorial tool for building maps between shift systems on directed graphs, and applies them to a classic group theory problem. Higman-Thompson groups can be viewed as the full symmetry groups of such shifts. Whether two of them are isomorphic was conjectured by Higman, and existence of the isomorphisms was later proved, but an explicit construction was missing.

Gluing diagrams construct homomorphisms between the shift pseudogroups, and the paper establishes which diagrams give isomorphisms. The constructive procedure for Higman-Thompson groups follows Euclid's algorithm, the ancient method for common divisors, repurposed as a recipe for gluing. The diagrams also lift isomorphisms to higher arity, giving explicit witnesses where theory previously gave only existence.
arxiv-2605-03689:
Mert Tiftikci, Amir Molzam Sharifloo, and Mira Mezini introduce CGFuse, a framework that gives pre-trained language models direct access to the structure of program code. Language models read code as token sequences, so they miss control flow and data dependencies that a graph represents naturally. Earlier fixes extracted graph features or added them to prompts, losing information along the way.

CGFuse instead fuses graph-derived representations at token level inside the model's intermediate layers. A graph neural network learns the structural features, and the language model keeps its fine-grained detail during generation. The authors present the work as the first systematic exploration of deep token-level graph-language fusion for structure-aware code generation.
arxiv-2605-03989:
Dutao Zhang and Tian Liao present Experience-RAG Skill, a pluggable retrieval layer that sits between an agent and a pool of retrievers in retrieval-augmented generation systems. A single fixed retrieval pipeline is often assumed to serve all tasks, yet factoid question answering, multi-hop reasoning, and scientific fact checking prefer different retrieval strategies. The skill chooses among them per task.

The proposed skill analyzes the current scene and consults an experience memory. It selects a suitable retrieval strategy and returns structured evidence to the agent. Under a fixed candidate pool, it achieved a strong overall ranking score across three BEIR datasets. Those cover natural questions, multi-hop questions, and scientific fact checking. It outperformed fixed single-retriever baselines and stayed close to Adaptive-RAG-style routing. The authors argue picking the retrieval strategy belongs in a reusable agent skill.
arxiv-2605-04189:
Brandon Lit, Anthony Maocheia-Ricci, and Thomas Driscoll compare how software testing tools show their results to the people who run them. Their study covers fifty tools and test harnesses across four well used programming languages, most with text output and a few with visual screens.

The team records the shared parts of these outputs, how results are laid out, and how colour is used in both text and visual tools. Their findings point to clear trends that tool makers can follow, so test results become easier to read, scan, and act on.
arxiv-2605-04289:
Andrea Britto and five co-authors build realistic models of United States power transmission grids entirely from public data. Detailed grid data are restricted for security reasons, which limits research, so an open route to full models has clear value.

Their five-stage pipeline pulls infrastructure from OpenStreetMap, rebuilds the network layout, estimates electrical values from official plant data, and spreads hourly demand across buses using census population. It then solves power flow for models of all forty-eight mainland states plus six multi-state regions. Most state models converge under the strictest settings, and costs and losses look close to real market outcomes.
arxiv-2605-04689:
Tao Gu and three co-authors explore a bridge between logic and computation, linking a completeness proof for intuitionistic logic to the programming technique of continuation-passing style. Their setting is proof-theoretic semantics, where the meaning of a logical statement is given by the rules for proving it.

They focus on base-extension semantics. They analyse a known completeness proof through the lenses of Kripke and Heyting semantics. They also use natural deduction and the lambda calculus, on the computing side. Their analysis shows that written forms of continuations capture basic ideas about meaning and use. Proof-theoretic semantics makes those ideas precise. The two traditions, they suggest, describe one thing from two sides.
arxiv-2605-04789:
Jun-Hua Gu and thirteen co-authors describe the design and commissioning of an upgraded radio telescope built as a testbed for the Square Kilometre Array era. Complex digital architectures in modern arrays create new instrumental effects, and strategies for handling them need a working platform before the giant array is fully operational.

The upgraded system adds a digital backend capable of forming beams in real time. The team demonstrates it with interferometric observations. High-time-resolution pulsar measurements confirm its sensitivity and stability. As a case study, they characterise a sawtooth-like spectral artefact. It is introduced by the two-stage channelisation used in similar low-frequency systems. They use both simulations and real data, to guide future calibration.
arxiv-2605-04889:
Robert Hao and three co-authors prove a new partition identity in the Andrews-Gordon family, which concerns ways of writing whole numbers as sums under set rules. Earlier work by Andrews treated parity conditions, where even or odd parts appear an even number of times. Two cases were settled, each with its own product form.

Hao and colleagues handle the remaining mixed-parity case using Bailey's lemma, obtaining an identity whose product side matches one earlier case. They also derive a recurrence by fixing peaks in related lattice paths, which supplies a combinatorial reading the sum form lacked. The identity is then proved analytically, completing this branch of the parity story.
arxiv-2605-04989:
Ali Shibli, Andrea Nascetti, and Yifang Ban test how best to adapt large geospatial foundation models for mapping wildfire burn areas from Sentinel-2 satellite images. Such maps support damage assessment, emissions modelling, and fire-climate research. The open question was which fine-tuning style survives shifts in place and time.

Using thousands of wildfire events across the United States and Canada, they compare full fine-tuning, decoder-only tuning, and low-rank adaptation for three leading models. Low-rank adaptation gave the strongest generalisation across domains while updating under one percent of parameters. One model paired with that method achieved the highest accuracy and the largest gain over full tuning.
arxiv-2605-05089:
Anatoly Krestenko and three co-authors treat decentralised basis trading, holding a spot asset while shorting its perpetual contract, as a collateral control problem. The strategy must split capital between spot inventory and derivative margin under on-chain liquidity and execution frictions. Getting that split wrong risks liquidation or wasted carry.

A static analysis shows a risk-constrained rule gives a more robust benchmark than the pure economic optimum, with required collateral rising under volatility stress. A dynamic extension sets an asymmetric intervention band, driven by solvency below and by carry losses versus rebalancing costs above. Live routed execution and historical backtests validate the execution layer of the design.
arxiv-2605-05189:
Nicholas Barnfield and four co-authors find sharp capacity limits for linear associative memories, asking how many key-value pairs a square matrix memory can store and retrieve. The answer depends on the retrieval rule, not just the number of free entries. Under Gaussian embeddings, they prove a sharp threshold for the strictest rule, where every target must beat its strongest competitor.

Above the threshold they construct a memory that retrieves everything, and below it they prove no data-dependent linear memory can. The logarithmic cost in the threshold is the unavoidable price of winner-take-all decoding. For weaker top-list retrieval they introduce a tail-average margin measure and characterise the high-dimensional behaviour of learning with it exactly.
arxiv-2605-05289:
Daniel Paradiso, Sarah Vallejo, and Eric Coughlin explain the origin of mass ejection in failed supernovae, the quiet collapses of massive stars that form black holes without a bright explosion. Neutrinos escaping the newborn neutron star launch a weak shock into the star's outer layers, producing a faint transient as it breaks out. Two self-similar solutions describe that shock, mixing outward ejecta with fallback onto the black hole.

The authors show the stronger-shock family is unstable, with its Mach number growing slowly away from the self-similar prediction, while the weaker family is stable. Above a reachable mass-loss threshold the shock strengthens toward the strong limit. Ejection, they conclude, is governed mainly by neutrino mass loss relative to the mass the shock encloses.
arxiv-2605-05589:
The Heisenberg chain is the textbook example of an exactly solvable quantum magnet. Oliver R. Bellwood and William J. Munro ask a sharper question: can its finite-size ground states be written down symbolically at all? They analyze exact Bethe ansatz solutions for chains of up to twelve sites, tracking the algebra behind the numbers.

The algebraic degree of the magnon phases and Bethe roots grows at a different rate than that of the energy and wavefunction. For ten or more sites, the Bethe roots and energy become Galois unsolvable. Exact solvability, in other words, does not guarantee a usable closed-form answer.
arxiv-2605-05689:
Diffusion models can predict how a graph will change, but sampling them is slow and sometimes unstable. Shaozhen Ma and four co-authors present GCCM, which pairs generative graph prediction with a contrastive consistency model. Consistency training shortens sampling to few steps, yet the authors find it can collapse into a shortcut that satisfies the constraint without learning the prediction.

Their contrastive component guards against that degenerate solution. The model learns conditional distributions over target graphs given an input graph. The combination aims at competitive accuracy with stable, cheap sampling at inference time.
arxiv-2605-05789:
Hiding secret text inside an image is an old trick with new stakes: hidden instructions can be aimed at large AI models. Zhen Sun and four co-authors build SADBench, a benchmark that stages this contest directly. It measures an attacker's ability to inject harmful secrets through steganography and a defender's ability to catch them through steganalysis.

The benchmark spans four core tasks covering both sides of the fight. Existing evaluations treated attack and defense separately or not at all. By scoring them together, SADBench shows how the threat evolves as each side improves.
arxiv-2605-06289:
Heegeon Yoon and Heeyoung Kim build a multimodal generative model for learning from partly labeled, class imbalanced data. Models trained on skewed data favor majority classes, and semi supervised learning makes it worse: pseudo labels for unlabeled items are predicted from the same skewed labeled set, spreading the bias further. Most existing remedies also assume a single input modality, ignoring the complementary signals that multimodal data offers.

Their model uses a separate encoder per modality with latent variables shared across modalities, joined by a product of experts rule. Student t distributions replace Gaussians in the prior, encoder, and decoder to fit the heavy tailed latent patterns of imbalanced data. A new training objective built on a power divergence covers labeled and unlabeled data together. Benchmark results beat baseline methods.
arxiv-2605-06389:
Cheng Chi and Yan Wang present a proof concerning families of sets with no s pairwise disjoint members. The maximum size of such a family is tied to the Erdős matching conjecture, a classic extremal combinatorics problem. Frankl and Kupavskii had conjectured an exact formula for a certain range of set sizes.

The authors show that, for each fixed m at least three and all sufficiently large s, the extremal families have a specific weighted form based on a small set L. That confirms the Frankl-Kupavskii conjecture in that range. For m equal to three they pin down the full range, extending earlier work.
arxiv-2605-06589:
Wilfrid Gangbo, Sebastian Munoz, Jeremy Wu, and Zhaoyu Zhang develop a careful solution theory for mean field game systems on finite graphs when individual noise is present. The extended system couples a master equation and a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation on the probability simplex. Its shape comes from discrete optimal transport, where an entropic equation appears as a gradient flow on the graph.

A key step proves positivity stays in a measured way for the discrete continuity equation, ruling out solutions hitting zero at the boundary in finite time. That yields smooth solutions on the open simplex with no boundary rule imposed. As an application, the discrete system recovers a Nash equilibrium reading through Markov chains on the graph.
arxiv-2605-06889:
Francisco Chen, Yiran Wang, and Yunpeng Shi improve global camera pose finding by enforcing consistency among triples of cameras. Structure-from-motion pipelines locate cameras from pairwise translation directions. Pairs estimated on their own can look locally plausible yet clash with each other. Their TriDE method treats triangle consistency as a cheap, higher-order check on each direction, avoiding a costly global nonlinear search that hinges on its starting point.

Message passing between directions and their weighted triangles refines weak estimates by spreading trustworthy information. The authors prove a phase-transition bound for exact recovery under a plausible corruption model. On real image graphs, direction accuracy improves by a large margin, and downstream camera locations get better. Local estimates thus link to global geometry in a practical way.
arxiv-2605-07289:
Soh Kumabe and Yuya Uezato study how hard it is to match text against regular expressions that contain backreferences, a feature of most real matching engines. The question matters because slow matching enables ReDoS attacks, where crafted input strings exhaust a server. Famous outages at Stack Overflow and Cloudflare came from exactly this weakness.

The pair prove strong limits. For the general problem, no algorithm can run much faster than a certain power of the input length, assuming a standard complexity hypothesis. The problem is also hard in a parameterized sense. For a restricted one-use form, though, they give a fast algorithm running in near-linear time. Their tools include suffix trees and factorization forests.
arxiv-2605-07389:
A. Azamnouri and five co-authors study teamwork problems inside machine learning teams in the semiconductor industry. Such teams mix engineers, data scientists, and domain experts with different goals and jargon, which makes long-term rollout harder. Hardware settings add strict data rules, long cycles, and tight coupling to plant processes.

Talking with twelve staff at a global chip company, the team found sixteen common challenges, with unclear roles and duties ranked most serious. They also collected habits staff found useful against those problems. The findings match known issues in cross-field work, but show how hardware constraints reshape them.
arxiv-2605-07789:
Sora Kang and six co-authors study how people actually make everyday decisions in conversation, to design conversational AI that works the way people do. Most systems reason from data, but people lean on heuristics and social moves in natural talk. The team analyzed nine hundred fifty-five real Korean conversations about food and travel decisions, coding them with a decision-making codebook.

People mostly satisfice rather than optimize, drawing on internal knowledge and conversational strategies to manage mental effort. A frequency-efficiency mismatch stood out: the commonest heuristics keep exploration flowing, while rare rule-based strategies are the ones that drive decisions to resolution when closing. The authors map how these patterns transfer to human-AI interaction and derive design lessons from them.
arxiv-2605-07889:
Louis Seyfritz and two co-authors hunt for warning signs before a giant solar flare. On October 3, 2024 the Sun produced an X9.0-class flare from active region NOAA 13842, and instruments had been watching for hours beforehand, a rare chance to study the pre-flare phase. The team analyzed spectroscopic data from the IRIS satellite, centered on a silicon emission line.

Time-series and wavelet analysis found two bands of periodic oscillation during the pre-flare hours, around seven to ten minutes and eighteen to twenty-one minutes, enhanced near the polarity inversion line. Line measures there also rose steadily from three hours before the flare, tipping into strong non-thermal velocities and blueshifts about fifteen minutes before onset. The pattern fits a slow destabilization of the coronal magnetic field, perhaps a flux rope activating, before rapid reconnection.
arxiv-2605-07989:
Wilhiam de Carvalho and four co-authors dissect dynamic operating envelopes: the import and export limits assigned to customers on radial distribution networks. They ask how the envelopes should be computed and shared out. As rooftop solar and electric vehicles stress low-voltage grids, these envelopes decide who may use how much network capacity. The calculation details turn out to matter a great deal.

Envelopes shift significantly with the power flow model used, with whether thermal or voltage limits bind, and with whether the import or export case is being computed. The team proposes a new algorithm, LACE, designed for transparent, scalable computation that can run on larger networks or alongside other optimization engines. Simulations span standard test feeders and a realistic Belgian low-voltage feeder with real-world data.
arxiv-2605-08289:
Fan Zhang, Shiming Fan, and Hua Wang argue that forecasting models should forget most cross-variable links. In multivariate series, real links depend on the current state. They also come with noise. Dense interaction layers can amplify fake correlations. They can smooth representations until predictions turn unreliable in the hard cases.

Their MS-FLOW framework treats interaction as a capacity-limited flow. The flow passes through a sparse bottleneck. Only a few key dependency paths stay open. Cross-variable signals pass under a strict communication budget. The routing keeps the links that matter for the present regime. It drops the spurious ones that dense models would amplify.
arxiv-2605-08389:
Mingyu Liu, Sihan Huang, Yijia Fan, Yinlin Yan, and coauthors fix a subtle flaw in zero-shot composed image retrieval. A user supplies a photo plus a text edit.
